title: Rethymno Food Guide: Where to Eat in the Old Town and on the Coast
seoTitle: Rethymno Food Guide: 5 Restaurants Worth Booking
seoDescription: Five restaurants that define eating in Rethymno - Prima Plora, Avli, Hasika, Alana and Taverna Galera - with what each does well and who it suits.
summary: Five restaurants cover the range of eating well in Rethymno: Prima Plora on the seafront for modern Mediterranean cooking with a view, Avli in a Venetian courtyard in the old town for refined Cretan cuisine, Hasika for straightforward Greek classics in a lively local room, Alana for a contemporary take on Cretan ingredients, and Taverna Galera for traditional, generous, no-frills Cretan cooking. Between them they span the whole spectrum from a special-occasion dinner to an ordinary long lunch, and all five sit within or beside the old town, so none of them needs a car. Book Prima Plora and Avli ahead in high season; the other three are easier to walk into.
body:
Rethymno rewards eating slowly. The old town is compact enough that you can walk between everything worth trying, and the coast is a few minutes away when you want a table with the sea in front of it. These five places are not a novelty list - they are the established ones, chosen for consistency rather than for being new.

## The five, side by side

| Restaurant | Cooking | Setting | Best for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Prima Plora | Modern Mediterranean, organic focus, strong wine list | On the seafront | A special dinner with a view |
| Avli | Cretan and Greek, traditional recipes with a gourmet hand | Venetian courtyard in the old town | Romantic dinners and a serious look at local gastronomy |
| Hasika | Classic Greek, cooked simply and well | Lively, informal, local | Honest food without formality |
| Alana | Contemporary Cretan, local products, modern technique | Stylish but comfortable | Creative cooking that still tastes of Crete |
| Taverna Galera | Traditional Cretan taverna cooking | Warm, unpretentious | A long, generous, no-frills meal |

## Prima Plora - elevated dining by the sea

Prima Plora is widely regarded as the best dining experience in Rethymno. It sits right on the seafront, and it pairs the view with modern Mediterranean cooking built on high-quality ingredients. The menu is creative without being pretentious, which is the harder thing to pull off, and the wine list is genuinely good. It is the meal people tend to remember at the end of a trip.

**Why it is worth the booking:** seafront location, creative Mediterranean cooking, high-end without being stiff.

## Avli - Cretan cuisine in a Venetian courtyard

Tucked into the heart of the old town, Avli is set in a traditional courtyard and feels both intimate and refined. The kitchen works with Cretan and Greek recipes, treating tradition seriously and paying close attention to detail. It suits anyone who wants to understand the depth of local gastronomy rather than just sample it, and it is one of the few restaurants in the city that is a destination in its own right.

**Why it is worth the booking:** traditional recipes with a gourmet touch, a historic setting, and a reputation earned over years.

## Hasika - the local favourite

Hasika has the reputation locals give a place they actually use. The menu is classic Greek, cooked simply and cooked well, in generous portions and with reliable quality. The room is lively, friendly and informal - close to what most travellers picture when they imagine a Greek restaurant. Come here for authentic flavours without any ceremony.

**Why it is worth the booking:** traditional Greek cooking, consistent quality, a warm local atmosphere.

## Alana - modern Cretan with character

Alana takes a contemporary approach to Cretan cooking without drifting away from its roots. Local products meet modern technique, and the dishes come out fresh, considered and well balanced. The setting is stylish but comfortable, which makes it a good middle option between a taverna and a formal dinner.

**Why it is worth the booking:** creative modern Cretan dishes, high-quality local ingredients, a fresh reading of familiar flavours.

## Taverna Galera - traditional hospitality

For the traditional end of the range, Taverna Galera does what a Cretan taverna is supposed to do. The food is hearty and rooted in recipes that have not needed changing, and meals are eaten slowly. If you want no-frills Cretan cooking and the hospitality that goes with it, this is the stop.

**Why it is worth the booking:** a genuine Cretan taverna, generous portions, warm service.

## Practical notes

- Greeks eat late. Tavernas fill from around 21:00 in summer; 19:30 is early enough to walk in almost anywhere.
- Book Prima Plora and Avli ahead between June and September. The other three are usually fine on the day.
- Raki arrives at the end of the meal, unasked and unbilled. It is a gesture rather than a course.
- All five are in or beside the old town, so you can walk to them; parking inside the old town is difficult and largely restricted.

Rethymno's dining scene reflects the island as a whole: rich in flavour, tied to history, and generous by default. These five are the culinary landmarks - the places that show you the city's identity through what it puts on a plate.

faqs.q: Where should I eat in Rethymno if I only have one dinner?
faqs.a: Avli if you want the old town and a Cretan menu treated seriously, or Prima Plora if you want the sea in front of you and modern Mediterranean cooking. Both should be booked ahead in summer.

faqs.q: Do I need to book restaurants in Rethymno?
faqs.a: Between June and September, book Prima Plora and Avli ahead. Hasika, Alana and Taverna Galera can usually take walk-ins, though arriving before 21:00 helps.

faqs.q: Are the old town restaurants walkable from the beach hotels?
faqs.a: Yes. All five sit in or beside the old town, and Rethymno's old town is small enough to cross on foot in about fifteen minutes. Driving in is the harder option - much of the old town is restricted and parking is scarce.

faqs.q: What should I order to eat like a local?
faqs.a: Dakos to start, then whatever the kitchen has cooked slowly that day - lamb or goat with herbs, or a vegetable stew. Finish with sfakian pie or the fruit and raki the house brings out.
